description: GitHub issue #30 comment 2026-08-25: 'To have hot reload by default in case I compile live in tex or typst' -- when the open PDF's file mtime changes on disk, automatically re-open it, preserving the current page index and zoom rather than snapping back to page 1. Polled (throttled, not every frame) rather than filesystem-watched, to avoid a new dependency (notify crate) for a desktop-only, not-latency-critical feature. Default ON per the explicit ask.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Implemented. crates/kovan/src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs:
- New "Hot reload" toggle (default ON per the explicit ask), checkbox in the toolbar.
- `check_hot_reload`: polls the open file's mtime, throttled to once per 500ms (RELOAD_CHECK_INTERVAL) via a stored Instant -- not filesystem-watched (no new `notify` dependency for a desktop-only, not-latency-critical feature). Calls `ctx.request_repaint_after(...)` so the check actually fires promptly even with no mouse/keyboard input (egui otherwise only repaints on input events, and a live TeX/Typst recompile producing a new file is not one).
- On a detected mtime change: re-opens the file and restores the page index the operator was looking at (clamped to the possibly-changed page count), so a live-editing loop doesn't snap back to page 1 on every save. Zoom is already preserved by the existing open-reset logic.
- Known, accepted limitation: annotations reset on reload (same as any fresh open) -- not attempted to be preserved/remapped against a changed document, given the added complexity for a live-compile-iteration use case where content is actively changing anyway.

3 new unit tests for the pure logic (`read_mtime`'s Some/None cases, `PdfReaderState::new()`'s default-on state). cargo check --all-targets clean (native + aarch64-linux-android). cargo test --release: 204 kovan lib tests passing. Not committed yet.

title: kovan-gui: PDF reader hot-reload (auto-refresh on file change, e.g. live TeX/Typst compile)
